sentences.text: THESE MFAs HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT ON 31.01.2023 COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:-
JUDGMENT

These appeals are arising out of a common judgment and award in MVC.No.92/2014 and 93/2014 on the file of I Addl.District and Sessions Judge & MACT, Raichur, whereby the claim petition filed by one Narayan and his son Mahesh were allowed in part granting compensation in a sum of Rs.5,60,000/- and Rs.30,000/- respectively with interest at 6% p.a. and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same.

entities.text: I Addl.District and Sessions Judge & MACT, Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
While MFA.No.200400/2018 and MFA.No.200401/2018 are filed by respondent No.2,
MFA.No.201079/2018 is filed by petitioner in MVC.No.93/2014 seeking enhancement of the compensation.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
4. FACTS:
It is the case of the petitioners that they are the father and son.

On 13.12.2012, at about 11.45 a.m, they were proceeding on TVS XL Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-36/H-8097 ('motor cycle' for short) towards Eklaspur of Raichur from their land situated at Merched village.
While the father was riding the motor cycle, his son aged about 12 years was the pillion rider.

At that time, the NEKRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-37/F- 421 ('offending vehicle' for short) came from Micro Tower side towards Raichur, driven by respondent No.1 in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
MFA No.201079 OF 2018 C/W MFA No.200400 OF 2018 MFA No.200401 OF 2018
As a result of the accident, both the petitioners sustained severe injuries.
The injuries sustained by petitioner- Narayan have resulted in permanent partial disability.
Despite prolonged treatment, they are not completely cured.
As the driver and owner-cum-internal insurer, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
5. Respondent No.2 has filed written statement denying that accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
At the time of accident, petitioner-Narayan was not holding a valid driving license and consequently, responsible for causing the accident.
The compensation claimed is highly exorbitant, fanciful and without any basis.
It is denied that the accidental injuries have resulted in permanent partial disability affecting income of the petitioner-Narayan and prays to dismiss the petition.

The Divisional vs Mahesh And Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141532848/
4 MFA No.201079 OF 2018 C/W MFA No.200400 OF 2018 MFA No.200401 OF 2018 6.
Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
7. Common evidence is recorded wherein petitioner Narayan has given evidence as PW-1 both on his behalf and also on behalf of his minor son.
PW-2 Doctor Pundalikappa is examined to prove the disability suffered by the petitioner Narayan.
Ex.P1 to 436 are marked.
8. On behalf of respondents, respondent No.1 is examined as RW-1.
No documents are marked on behalf of respondents.

9. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petitions granting compensation in a sum of Rs.5,60,000/- to petitioner Narayan and Rs.30,000/- to petitioner Mahesh.

The details of compensation granted by the Tribunal to petitioner- Narayan is as below:
MFA No.201079 OF 2018 C/W MFA No.200400 OF 2018 MFA No.200401 OF 2018 Heads Amount in Rs.
 Pain and Suffering 30,000  Loss of future earning 3,15,000  For medical expenses based on 1,00,000
Medical bills and evidence  Loss of income 1,00,000  Towards attendance charge & 15,000  special food & diet and also  Transportation charges  Total 5,60,000 10.

Challenging the impugned judgment and award, respondent No.2 has filed MFA.No.200400/2018 and MFA.No.200401/2018 contending that at the time of accident, the rider of the motor cycle i.e., petitioner Narayan was not possessing a valid driving license.
The motor cycle was also not covered by a valid policy.
Consequently, he has contributed towards the cause of the accident.
Having regard to the fact that PW-2 is not a treating Doctor, the Tribunal has erred in considering the whole body disability at 35% and prays to allow the appeals and reduce the compensation.
In MFA.No.201079/2018, petitioner Narayan has contended that he has sustained whole body disability at 70% and therefore, the Tribunal has erred in considering it as 35% of the whole body.
The compensation granted under all the heads is on the lower side.

The Tribunal has not granted any compensation under the head 'loss of amenities of life' and prays to allow the appeal and The Divisional vs Mahesh And Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141532848/
5 enhance the compensation.

12. Heard arguments and perused the record.
13.
In respect of the accident, complaint was lodged by petitioner-Narayan on the same day at 12.30 p.m.
In the complaint, he has stated that accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
After completion of investigation, the concerned police have filed charge sheet against respondent No.1.
Admittedly, respondent No.1 has not challenged the charge sheet.

Except making allegations that accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner-Narayan, there is no MFA No.201079 OF 2018 C/W MFA No.200400 OF 2018 MFA No.200401 OF 2018 material to substantiate the same.
Moreover, respondents have not taken any steps to ascertain whether petitioner- Narayan was holding a valid driving license or not.
Even in the absence of such license, there is no presumption that it was the cause for the accident.
In the light of charge sheet being filed against respondent No.1, the contentions of respondents that petitioner-Narayan has contributed towards the cause of accident cannot be accepted.

14. So far as compensation granted in MVC.No.92/2014 is concerned, taking into consideration the nature of injury suffered and the treatment taken, the Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.30,000/-.
15. So far as the compensation in respect of the injuries sustained by petitioner-Narayan as sought in MVC.No.93/2014, in the claim petition petitioner has shown his age as 40 years.
In the medical records, his age is noted as 42 years.
It is pertinent to note that in respect of MFA No.201079 OF 2018 C/W MFA No.200400 OF 2018 MFA No.200401 OF 2018 accident, complaint is given by petitioner Narayan himself.

In the said complaint, at the earliest available opportunity, petitioner has given his age as 45 years and he has not chosen to produce any other documents such as Aadhaar card or other documents to show his exact age.
Therefore, his age is taken as 45 years as against 40 years taken by the Tribunal.
Consequently, the appropriate multiplier would be 14 as against 15 taken by the Tribunal.
16. Though he has claimed that per month he used to earn Rs.7,500/- and also Rs.1,40,000/- per year from agriculture, he has not produced any documents to prove the same.
Therefore, the Tribunal has taken his income as Rs.5,000/- p.m. on notional basis.
Having regard to the fact that the accident is of the year, based on minimum wages, notional income ought to have been taken at Rs.6,500/- per month.
PW-2 has deposed that petitioner has sustained 70% disability of the whole body.
He is not a treated Doctor.

Consequently, 1/3rd of the disability calculated by PW-2 is required to be taken and the same is quantified at MFA No.201079 OF 2018 C/W MFA No.200400 OF 2018 MFA No.200401 OF 2018 25% instead of 35% taken by the Tribunal.
As per decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma General Insurance Co.Ltd case, 25% of the income is required to be added towards 'loss of future prospects'.
Therefore, for calculating compensation for 'loss of income due to permanent partial disability' the notional income of the petitioner is required to be taken at Rs.8,125/- per month.

With these components,
compensation under the head 'loss of income due to disability' is Rs.8,125 x 12 x 14 x 25% =
Rs.3,41,250/- as against Rs.3,15,000/- granted by the Tribunal.
The Divisional vs Mahesh And Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141532848/
6 17.

Based on medical bills, the Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
under the head medical expenses and it does not call for any interference.
18. The Tribunal has not granted any compensation under the head 'loss of amenities of life'.

Taking into consideration the injury sustained and the fact that they MFA No.201079 OF 2018 C/W MFA No.200400 OF 2018 MFA No.200401 OF 2018 have resulted in permanent partial disability, this Court is of the considered opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/- under the head 'pain and suffering' as against Rs.30,000/- granted by the Tribunal and also Rs.30,000/- towards 'loss of amenities of life'.

19. The Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.15,000/- under the head 'attendant charges, special food, diet and also transportation charges', it will also not call for any interference.
20. The Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- under the head 'loss of income'.
It appears this compensation is granted towards 'loss of income during laid up period'.

Since the notional income of petitioner is to be considered at Rs.6,500/- taking into consideration the nature of injury suffered and period of treatment, it would be reasonable to expect that he was under treatment for a period of three months.

Therefore, at the rate of Rs.6,500/-
MFA No.201079 OF 2018 C/W MFA No.200400 OF 2018 MFA No.200401 OF 2018 for a period of three months, petitioner is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.19,500/- under the head 'loss of income during laid up period' as against Rs.1,00,000/- granted by the Tribunal.

21. Thus, in all petitioner is entitled for a compensation in a sum of Rs.5,45,750/- as against Rs.5,60,000/- granted by the Tribunal as detailed below:
 Heads Amount Amount  granted by granted by  the Tribunal this Court  In Rs. In Rs.
 Pain and Suffering 30,000 40,000  Loss of future earning 3,15,000 3,41,250  For medical expenses 1,00,000 1,00,000  based on Medical bills  and evidence  Loss of income during 1,00,000 19,500  laid up period  Towards attendance 15,000 15,000  charge & special food &
 diet and also  Transportation charges  Loss of amenities - 30,000  Total 5,60,000 5,45,750

The Divisional vs Mahesh And Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141532848/
7 22.

In the result, MFA.No.200400/2018 filed by respondent No.2 and MFA.No.201079/2018 filed by MFA No.201079 OF 2018 C/W MFA No.200400 OF 2018 MFA No.200401 OF 2018 petitioner are liable to be rejected and MFA.No.200401/2018 filed by respondent No.2 is allowed in part and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) MFA.No.200400/2018 filed by respondent No.2 and MFA.No.201079/2018 filed by the petitioner are dismissed.
(ii) MFA.No.200401/2018 filed by respondent  No.2 is allowed.

The petitioner in  MVC.No.93/2014 is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.5,45,750/-
together with interest at 6% p.a as against Rs.5,60,000/- granted by the Tribunal.
(iii) The Registry is directed to transmit the amount in deposit (if any) to the Tribunal.
(iv) The Registry is also directed to send back the trial court records along with the copy of this judgment to the Tribunal forthwith.

Sd/-
